simple: Palo Alto Networks virtual next-generation firewalls: the same PAN-OS capabilities as the hardware PA-Series, as a virtual machine for your own data center and private clouds (VMware ESXi, KVM and others) as well as public clouds (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud) — to protect traffic between applications and segments inside the cloud; licensed with Software NGFW credits, bring-your-own-license or pay-as-you-go. Identifies applications (App-ID), users and devices, decrypts TLS and connects sites over IPsec VPN; managed with Panorama or Strata Cloud Manager. On this site we assume the firewall comes with two subscriptions by default. The Precision AI Network Security bundle: Advanced Threat Prevention — an intrusion prevention system (IPS) that blocks exploits, spyware and even unknown command-and-control (C2) channels inline; Advanced WildFire — a cloud sandbox that checks unknown files; Advanced URL Filtering — real-time website analysis that blocks phishing and malicious pages; Advanced DNS Security — blocks dangerous domains, DNS tunnels and malware-generated domains (DGA); Advanced IP Defense — blocks attacker infrastructure by IP; Device Security — discovers and classifies IoT and other unmanaged devices on the network; Advanced SD-WAN. The Prisma Access Agent subscription — an agent for employee remote access through the firewall (it replaces the GlobalProtect gateway license).
